paper.title: Partial Routing: Trace-Tuned Delegation for Resource-Efficient Agentic Workflows

claims.text: Partial routing profiles solo traces of a lead and a worker model into recurring subtasks with measured cost and quality, then compiles them into a delegation policy whose aggressiveness is set by a parameter delta; it needs no training.
At delta=0.75, partial routing beats the lead alone on ViBench (higher score at lower cost) and on Terminal-Bench (higher pass rate at similar cost).
Task-level routers (the hindsight oracle and Jev) score lower than partial routing on ViBench, and they cost more.
Unguided delegation to a cheaper worker already helps on ViBench, and partial routing adds a further gain over it.
Giving the lead only the profiled subtask plan, with no worker, cuts cost on both benchmarks at a similar or higher score.
On Terminal-Bench the gain is in quality, not cost.
LLM-judge quality scores are stable across re-runs.
A second model pair on each benchmark points to gains that carry over, though each pair ran only once.

The advantage over unguided delegation on ViBench is much larger on the profiling applications than on the held-out ones, which points to some overfitting of the profile to the applications it came from.

limits_authors.text: The main results use one model pair per benchmark, with few tasks and runs.
The second model pairs ran once, compared only against the two solo models.
Untested for pairs with smaller capability or price gaps.
Sensitivity to rho, tau and the number of profiling tasks was not studied.
The annotator's and judge's labels were not validated against human labels.
Whether the lead followed its assigned tiers was not checked systematically.
Delegation increases wall-clock time a lot.

likely_overclaims: The claim of higher performance than all baselines rests on very small held-out sets with only a few runs and no significance tests; on Terminal-Bench the margin over the oracle and the plan-only lead amounts to roughly one task.

delta was chosen among a few values directly on the held-out sets rather than on a separate validation set, even though the authors recommend validation sweeps; lower delta values scored below the lead alone on ViBench.
The idea that the workers' gain comes from context management is a hypothesis the paper does not test.
Calling the overhead small counts only the LLM profiling calls; it leaves out the cost of the solo rollouts the profiling needs and the large wall-clock slowdown.
The paper calls its approach uniquely dynamic, informed and controllable, but that rests on the authors' own categorisation of prior approaches.
The authors disclose that Replit, the source of the ViBench workloads, is a portfolio company of their firm, which is a possible conflict of interest.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Partial routing. Offline, the lead and the worker each do the same tasks alone, and an LLM annotator then tags each step of their rollouts (gray) with a recurring subtask from a set \mathcal{S}; an LLM judge scores both models on each subtask, and \delta turns quality and cost saving into delegation tiers. Online, the lead follows this policy and briefs a fresh worker whenever it hands off a subtask.
Figure 2: Cost and quality on the ten held-out ViBench applications, mean of three runs.
Figure 3: Cost and pass rate on the 23 held-out Terminal-Bench tasks, mean of two runs per task.

change_for_agents: Rather than routing a whole task to one model, builders can mine logged traces for recurring subtasks, measure the quality and cost gaps on each, and put tiered delegation guidance (delegate, conditional or keep) in the lead agent's prompt, with no training. Even the subtask plan alone, without a worker, can cut cost. Expect longer wall-clock times when delegating.

compact.claim: Trace-profiled, prompt-level guidance for delegating subtasks from a frontier lead to a cheap worker beats both the lead alone and task-level routing on long coding tasks.
compact.method: An LLM annotator labels solo rollouts of both models with recurring subtasks, and an LLM judge scores each model's quality on each subtask. Cost savings and quality risk are combined through delta into delegate/conditional/keep tiers, which go into the lead's prompt alongside a delegation tool.

results.finding: At delta=0.75 on ViBench, score rises from 70.2 to 78.5 at 19% lower cost; on Terminal-Bench, the pass rate rises from 54% to 61% at similar cost.
Partial routing adds 2.9 points over unguided delegation on ViBench.
The subtask plan alone cuts the lead's cost by 39% on ViBench and 16% on Terminal-Bench.
Judge quality scores vary by at most 0.3 points across re-runs.

compact.limits: One main model pair per benchmark, small held-out sets, few runs, fixed hyperparameters, and no human validation of the LLM annotator and judge.
